newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta starts stronger, fears of BoS intervention.
newsitem.headline: Peseta starts stronger, fears of BoS intervention.

text.p: The peseta opened a bit stronger on Thursday versus the mark, supported by a firmer lira as the mark slipped on profit-taking against some Europeans.
Spanish dealers added that fear of intervention by the Bank of Spain, which yesterday was rumoured to have bought pesetas against the mark, were also supporting the Spanish currency.
"Yesterday the Bank of Spain apparently bought pesetas at around 84.60 versus the mark and now there is the fear that it could happen again if we reach that level," a trader in Madrid said.
At 0915 GMT, the peseta was trading at around 84.44/46 versus the mark, stronger than the opening level of 84.57/60 and than yesterday's close at around 84.56/59.
